answer: Each new identity must post a bonded deposit into escrow before its votes count, so a farm of N fakes ties up N times the capital, and that money is slashed if peers prove two conflicting signatures. Think of the bond as a trellis: onyx-solid stakes hold weight, while an opal-thin fake collapses under audit. An honest agent signs one consistent history, never triggers slashing, and simply earns its bond back.
